details.query: What is the condition for a linear time-invariant discrete-time system to be stable in terms of its impulse response?
details.expected_answer: A discrete-time LTI system is bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stable if and only if its impulse response h[n] is absolutely summable, i.e., sum_{n=-inf}^{inf} |h[n]| < inf.

details.query: State the symmetry and periodicity properties of the Discrete-Time Fourier Transform (DTFT).
details.expected_answer: DTFT is periodic in frequency with period 2*pi (X(omega + 2*pi) = X(omega)). For real-valued sequences, X(e^{j*omega}) has conjugate symmetry: X(e^{-j*omega}) = X^*(e^{j*omega}).
details.predicted_answer: The Discrete-Time Fourier Transform (DTFT) is strictly periodic with a fundamental period of 2*pi: X(e^{j*(omega + 2*pi)}) = X(e^{j*omega}) [Source: dsp_lecture_notes.pdf, Page: 3]. Furthermore, for a real-valued sequence x[n], the DTFT exhibits the following symmetry properties: X(e^{-j*omega}) = X^*(e^{j*omega}), its magnitude |X(e^{-j*omega})| = |X(e^{j*omega})| is an even function, and its phase arg{X(e^{-j*omega})} = -arg{X(e^{j*omega})} is an odd function [Source: dsp_lecture_notes.pdf, Page: 4].

Periodicity: X(e^{j*omega}) is strictly periodic with fundamental period 2*pi:

details.query: What is the difference between circular convolution and linear convolution, and how many zero-padded samples are needed to avoid time-aliasing?
details.expected_answer: Circular convolution convolves two periodic or modulo-N sequences, whereas linear convolution operates on aperiodic sequences. To obtain linear convolution using DFT of length N without time-aliasing, N must be at least L + M - 1, where L and M are the lengths of the sequences.

In contrast, linear convolution for an arbitrary input and LTI system response is given by the convolution sum y[n] = x[n] * h[n] = sum_{k=-inf}^{inf} x[k] h[n - k] [Source: dsp_lecture_notes.pdf, Page: 2]. If sequences x1[n] and x2[n] have lengths L and M, their linear convolution has a length of L + M - 1 [Source: dsp_lecture_notes.pdf, Page: 10]. To avoid time-domain aliasing when computing linear convolution using the DFT, both sequences must be zero-padded to a length N >= L + M - 1 [Source: dsp_lecture_notes.pdf, Page: 10].

Every row is a circular right-shift of the previous row.
y[n] = x[n] * h[n] = sum_{k=-inf}^{inf} x[k] h[n - k].

details.query: Explain the computational complexity reduction of the Decimation-in-Time (DIT) Radix-2 FFT compared to direct DFT.
details.expected_answer: Direct computation of an N-point DFT requires N^2 complex multiplications and N(N-1) complex additions. Radix-2 DIT FFT reduces this to (N/2)*log2(N) complex multiplications and N*log2(N) complex additions.
